given: the stock table holds a set of existing rows before the migration
when: the up migration runs to completion (or fails partway and rolls back)
then: every pre-existing row survives with unchanged identity and unchanged canonical location, the row count is preserved with no row lost or corrupted, and if any step fails the whole migration rolls back leaving the table exactly as it was
architectural_notes: Infra atomic no-data-loss guarantee realized by PI1-migration-atomic (transactional): the add -> backfill -> drop up migration runs as a single atomic unit so either every row survives with unchanged identity and canonical location or the whole migration rolls back. This is the genuine row-survival guarantee of NFR-F6-1 over an EXISTING table. The UNIQUE(sku, location) key (PI4-unique-sku-location-preserved) stays untouched because location is not recreated. Verified by an R4/NFR-F6-4 real-branch round-trip test asserting preserved row count and per-row identity/location; tests T8/T9 cite PI1-migration-atomic.

independence.rationale: AC1/AC2 assert the per-field backfill transform value; AC3 asserts whole-table survival and atomicity. Row-count/identity survival can break (a lost or corrupted row, or a partial non-atomic apply) while the per-field backfill is correct, and vice versa
